correctness.rationale: Computed the sole nonzero singular value of rank-one P_u P_v and recovered D_p=sqrt(2)F_p(theta) with Fubini-Study angular distance. Re-differentiated the curvature numerator; at p=2/3 it is (2/3)(1-z)^3(1+z), z=cos(theta)^(2/3). Verified the L2 integral convex-composition step for smaller exponents, and the derivative-ratio weighted-average argument showing the endpoint supremum of F_p(s)/(2F_p(s/2)) is attained at s=pi/2. The two cases theta(P,Q)+theta(Q,R)<=pi/2 and >pi/2 prove the global inequality. Strict Jensen plus monotone ratio forces midpoint equality; Taylor coefficient (2-3p)/24 proves nonconvexity for p>2/3 near zero. An independent symbolic identity check and 3,000 sampled ray triples corroborate, not replace, these unrestricted steps. Zero angle, orthogonal boundary and p->0 limit are handled.

value.rationale: Sharp all-dimensional distortion for a natural family of quantum pure-state dissimilarities quantifies exactly how triangle inequality fails, beyond a binary counterexample. The extremal geometry and sharp p=2/3 convexity boundary are natural analytic structure useful in quasi-metric comparisons. final_claim: For every complex Hilbert space of dimension at least 2 and rank-one projections, D_p(P,Q)=[2-2|<u,v>|^p]^{1/2} has the exact quasi-triangle distortion K_p=(2 sqrt(1-2^{-p/2}))^{-1} for every 0<p<=2/3. Orthogonal endpoint rays with a projective pi/4 midpoint attain it. F_p(theta)=sqrt(1-cos^p theta) is convex precisely for 0<p<=2/3 within 0<p<1.
